object_description: compact cross-stacked blocks around courtyards and cavities
design_condition: Three cross-stacked blocks are placed centrally within the perimeter, creating a tree-lined western square and diverse elevated outdoor spaces while preserving eastern room for future expansion.

positive.statement: The sophisticated staggering fits very well into the urban planning situation.
The project offers a spacious and attractively designed entrance area, courtyards and terraces.
The different levels and open and covered conditions create a diverse range of stay options.
The incidence of natural light in large parts of the teaching areas offers a very special quality.
The networking of the building parts creates a variety of visual relationships.
The facade expression authentically reflects the building's use and gives the ensemble an appropriate scale.
The large building volume is convincingly integrated into its surroundings, with harmonious proportions.

negative.statement: The three-dimensional building grid dictates the internal organization in a strong and almost cartoonish way.
The multiplication of vertical axes makes orientation through the building complex very difficult.
Flexibility of use is limited by the resulting arrangement of usable areas.
The structural concept becomes relatively complex because of the many projections, recesses and volumetric gimmicks.
The delivery of materials to the special-use areas and workshops is not optimal.
Construction and maintenance costs are expected to be above average.
